title: runtime: add kernel registry schema v1 + versioned table loader (initial Llama/Mistral/Qwen entries)
author: Grace Kim
description: Motivation: Kernel selector v2 needs a data-driven registry to decouple “which kernel should we use” from selector logic and to make selections reviewable + reproducible across GPU SKUs. This PR introduces kernel registry schema v1, a versioned loader/validator, and a small initial selection table covering the top model families (Llama/Mistral/Qwen) across L4/A10/A100/H100 for a limited set of seq-length buckets. Scope notes: (1) This PR does not change default runtime behavior; selector v1 remains the default and selector v2 is still gated behind the feature flag. (2) The table is intentionally small and biased toward safe, well-tested kernels to reduce correctness risk while the rest of v2 lands. What’s included: Schema v1: A stable, versioned file format for mapping (model_family, regime, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_class) -> kernel_id (+ optional attrs). Loader: Parses registry files at startup, validates schema/version, and exposes an in-memory map for selector v2. Validation rules: required fields, allowed enums, duplicate key detection, and “safe kernel set” constraints for unknown model families. Versioning strategy: semantic-ish “registry_version” with explicit compatibility checks; schema version is separate from registry content version to allow table updates without code changes. Initial table: Llama-family / Mistral-family / Qwen-family entries for common buckets: prefill: {0-512, 513-2k, 2k-8k}; decode: {<=128, 129-512}. GPUs: {L4, A10, A100-80G, H100}. Kernel ids are existing runtime kernel implementations (no new kernels). Testing: unit tests for parser/validator, golden tests for deterministic lookup, and a small conformance smoke that asserts the referenced kernels exist in the runtime kernel catalog. Rollout plan: ship registry loader in runtime-1.19 behind the selector v2 flag; table updates will be done via follow-on PRs as we benchmark/expand coverage. Follow-ups: (a) add more families + more buckets once benchmark-lab results are in, (b) integrate overrides/patch-layer semantics (ENG-3931), (c) add metrics for registry hit/miss and fallback reasons (ENG-3927).

conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can we be explicit about what happens when the registry file is missing / invalid at startup? I don’t want serving to fail hard for hosted if config rollout is partial.

Grace Kim (author): Yep. Loader is “best-effort” when selector v2 is disabled. When v2 is enabled, we still don’t crash the process; we mark registry_state=invalid and selector v2 returns a structured fallback reason and delegates to v1. I added a unit test to cover invalid YAML + unknown fields behavior.
Yuki Sato (review): For GPU matching: A100-40G vs A100-80G vs MIG. Schema currently has gpu_sku_class={A100,H100,L4,A10}. Is that too coarse? We’ll want partition-awareness eventually.

Grace Kim (author): Agree long-term. For v1 schema I kept it intentionally coarse to avoid table explosion + card risks. The loader maps detailed GPU SKU -> sku_class (existing normalization logic is landing in a separate PR). I added comments in the schema and a TODO for MIG/partition class once we have stable normalization output.
Hiro Tanaka (review): Kernel ids: are these stable? If we rename kernel implementations we’ll silently break lookups.

Grace Kim (author): Added a referenced-kernel existence test that fails build if any registry entry points at a missing kernel id. Also added guidance in kernel_registry_update_process.md: kernel ids are treated as API-stable; rename requires a compatibility alias for at least one release.
Thomas Baird (review): Please avoid unbounded enums/strings that will become telemetry labels later. Any chance “model_family” should be an enum rather than free-form string?

Grace Kim (author): In schema v1, model_family is an enum with a reserved UNKNOWN. The mapping logic from model metadata -> family is separate, but registry keys are restricted. Added validator checks to reject unrecognized families (unless explicitly set to UNKNOWN for safe fallback entries).
Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you clarify precedence if multiple rows match (e.g., missing gpu match falls back to DEFAULT)?

Grace Kim (author): Added explicit lookup order in lookup.rs and in docs: exact (family, regime, bucket, sku_class) then (family, regime, bucket, DEFAULT) then (family, regime, DEFAULT, DEFAULT) then UNKNOWN family safe set. Tie-breaking is deterministic by specificity score.
Noah Patel (approval): LGTM after the fallback behavior clarification + tests. This unblocks selector v2 landing cleanly.
Hiro Tanaka (approval): Approved. Please keep the initial table conservative; we can expand once conformance coverage is broader.
Yuki Sato (approval): Approved with note: follow up on MIG/partition handling once normalization PR is merged.
release_notes: Internal: runtime now supports loading a versioned kernel registry table (schema v1) for kernel selector v2; no behavior change unless selector v2 is enabled.
